features.title: /stx-fix writes a per-fix folder with fix-report.html and fix-state.json
features.actor: developer running /stx-fix against a reproducible bug
acceptance_criteria: Running /stx-fix to completion against a known bug creates a directory at docs/waves/fix-{slug}/ where {slug} is derived from the bug title (kebab-case, same slug rule already used by /stx-fix for branch naming).

The folder name is literally fix-{slug} (no random suffix, no timestamp suffix). If a folder with the same slug already exists, the orchestrator surfaces this rather than silently overwriting — the chosen collision-handling strategy is an Architect decision but the chosen behavior MUST be documented in stx-fix/SKILL.md.

Inside docs/waves/fix-{slug}/, exactly two files are written: fix-state.json (canonical machine-readable state for that fix run) and fix-report.html (rendered human-readable report). No prompt snapshot file is written.

fix-state.json contains at minimum: a fix_id, fix_slug, status (one of done | halted-at-cap | blocked | cancelled), started_at, finished_at, the rendered template fields (title, issues, repro, expected, scope_hints, out_of_scope, test_kind, iteration_cap, commit_policy), the iteration count actually consumed, and references to the failing test files written by QA and the production files touched by Coder.

fix-report.html is self-contained (offline-renderable, inline styles) and visually consistent with the existing /stx-feature wave artifacts (reuses _styles.html-equivalent typography, colors, card and status conventions).
Both files are written before /stx-fix's existing terminal summary is printed.
The last line of the terminal summary printed by /stx-fix is `Report written to <abs-path-to-fix-report.html>` (the existing in-conversation terminal summary is otherwise preserved unchanged).

Halt paths (iteration cap tripped, Coder edits a test file, user cancels at the acceptance gate before Step 6, etc.) still write fix-state.json with the appropriate non-done status, and a fix-report.html that reflects the halted state. The orchestrator never silently skips the artifact write.
The new behavior is default — no flag is required to turn it on, and no flag turns it off.
out_of_scope: Adding a random-suffix or timestamp-suffix to the fix folder name — the name is literally fix-{slug}.
Adding a --report or --no-report flag to /stx-fix — the artifact write is unconditional.
Writing a prompt-snapshot file inside fix-{slug}/ — only fix-report.html and fix-state.json are written.
Changing the QA → Coder loop semantics, the iteration caps, or any halt conditions.
Changing the Coder's prohibition on editing test files, or the QA/Coder separation rule.
Mid-loop streaming of fix-report.html as a live dashboard — the report is written at fix-end (or halt), not per-iteration.

features.title: fix-wiki.html cross-fix index (sibling of wave-wiki.html)
features.actor: developer browsing docs/waves/ to see all past fixes at a glance
acceptance_criteria: After /stx-fix completes (done or halted) and writes its per-fix folder per F1, a separate aggregator file at docs/waves/fix-wiki.html is rebuilt from scratch by scanning every docs/waves/fix-*/fix-state.json.

fix-wiki.html visually mirrors the existing docs/waves/wave-wiki.html — same header eyebrow + serif H1, same INLINE_STYLES block from _styles.html, same single-table layout sorted by started_at DESC, same status pill classes.
The fix-wiki table includes one row per fix-*/ folder regardless of status (done | halted-at-cap | blocked | cancelled) so the table doubles as a live dashboard.
Each row in fix-wiki.html links to the corresponding ./fix-{slug}/fix-report.html (or ./fix-{slug}/ if the report file is missing).

fix-wiki.html is idempotent: deleting a fix-*/ folder and re-running any /stx-fix removes that row; manually creating a fix-*/ folder with a valid fix-state.json adds a row. The file is never hand-edited and never appended-to in place.

The existing wave-wiki.html scan is tightened so it only picks up wave-*/ folders (matching pattern wave-<slug>-<4-char-suffix>/wave-state.json). fix-*/ folders must NOT appear as rows in wave-wiki.html, and wave-*/ folders must NOT appear as rows in fix-wiki.html.
fix-wiki.html and the wave-wiki.html scan-tightening are part of /stx-fix's close-out — they do NOT require also re-running /stx-feature.
Header copy on fix-wiki.html is distinct from wave-wiki.html so a casual reader can tell them apart at a glance.
out_of_scope: Extending wave-wiki.html to also list fix-*/ folders — the user explicitly chose two separate wikis.
Adding filters, search, or sort controls to either wiki — both stay as plain HTML tables.
Changing the visual look of wave-wiki.html beyond the scan-glob tightening.
Adding a feed (RSS / JSON) or an API for cross-fix data.
